## Research question

Will specially constructed asymmetric triggers at inference time\u2014such as low-opacity triggers\u2014adversarially bypass BaDExpert\u2019s detection by altering trigger characteristics compared to those used during model production?

## Agent instructions

Design an experiment that mirrors the adaptive attack settings  1) Prepare a controlled subset of the backdoor dataset and generate adversarial examples using two types of modified triggers: (a) low-opacity triggers created by blending backdoor patterns with normal images at a reduced opacity level, and (b) optimized asymmetric triggers as in the BaDExpert-Adap-BadNet attack that minimizes the activation of the backdoor expert model. 2) Run these adversarial examples through the BaDExpert detection pipeline, ensuring that the model configuration and experimental setup follow the protocols used in prior experiments. 3) Record the key performance metrics\u2014Attack Success Rate (ASR) and Area Under the ROC Curve (AUROC)\u2014for each modified trigger condition. 4) Compare these metrics against scenarios using standard triggers. 5) Use the results, such as the observed AUROC values (~98.4% for low-opacity triggers and ~87.0% for the BaDExpert-Adap-BadNet attack) along with corresponding ASR values, to assess the degradation in detection performance and quantify the resilience of BaDExpert under these adaptive conditions.

Your task is to implement a system to test the BaDExpert defense against adaptive backdoor attacks. The system consists of three main components:

1. First, create a script to generate a poisoned dataset with adaptive backdoor attacks. The script should:
   - Support different datasets (CIFAR10, GTSRB, Imagenette)
   - Implement two types of adaptive attacks:
     a) An adaptive blend attack with low-opacity triggers (using a reduced alpha value like 0.05)
     b) An adaptive patch attack with optimized asymmetric triggers
   - Allow configuration of poison rate, target class, and trigger parameters
   - Save the poisoned dataset with appropriate metadata (images, labels, poison indices)

2. Next, create a script to train a model on the poisoned dataset. The script should:
   - Load the poisoned dataset created in step 1
   - Set up a neural network model appropriate for the dataset
   - Train the model using standard training procedures
   - Evaluate the model on both clean and poisoned test data
   - Save the trained model for later evaluation

3. Finally, implement the BaDExpert defense and evaluation script. The defense should:
   - Load the backdoored model from step 2
   - Create two expert models:
     a) An unlearned model: trained to give different predictions than the original model
     b) A shadow model: finetuned on clean data to maintain normal behavior
   - Implement a detection mechanism that compares the prediction patterns of the three models
   - Use the "triangle" metric to identify backdoored inputs
   - Evaluate and report defense performance using metrics like Attack Success Rate (ASR) and Area Under ROC Curve (AUROC)

The scripts should be designed to work together in sequence, with the output of each step serving as input to the next. Include appropriate command-line arguments to configure the experiments.
